title: How a Smartphone Touchscreen Works in 60 Seconds 📱👆 #shorts
description:
Your phone's screen can feel your finger without being pressed. Under the glass sits an invisible grid of transparent electrodes; your finger pulls a little electric charge away from the spot you touch, and a controller scans the grid over a hundred times a second to find it. Grid, touch, scan, pinpoint. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#touchscreen #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: The Screen
steps.text: Your phone screen can feel your finger, without you *pressing* at all.

steps.label: Hidden Grid
steps.text: Under the glass sits an invisible *grid* of see-through electrodes, in rows and columns.

steps.label: Electric Field
steps.text: Each crossing holds a tiny *electric field*, like millions of little capacitors.

steps.label: Your Finger
steps.text: Your body conducts electricity. A touch pulls away a bit of *charge* right at that spot.

steps.label: The Scan
steps.text: A controller *scans* every row and column, over a hundred times a second, and finds the dip.

steps.label: Gloves
steps.text: That's why normal *gloves* don't work. They block your finger's charge.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Grid, touch, scan, *pinpoint*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
